requirements.requirement: Export /srv/nfs/shared from node1 as an NFS share.
requirements.summary: node1 has an active, enabled NFS server; the configured and active export is /srv/nfs/shared, restricted to node2. It remained active after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Mount the node1 share at /mnt/shared on node2.
requirements.summary: node2 directly shows /mnt/shared mounted from node1:/srv/nfs/shared as NFSv4. The mount recovered automatically after both node restarts and supported subsequent reads and writes.

requirements.requirement: Provide the dataops identity with UID and GID 4500 on both systems.
requirements.summary: Direct identity queries on both nodes show dataops with UID 4500 and primary GID 4500, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set the shared directory to dataops:dataops mode 2770 and preserve consistent ownership and permissions for files created from either system.
requirements.summary: Both server and client views show the shared directory as dataops:dataops, numeric 4500:4500, mode 2770. Files created from node1 and node2 are visible cross-node with ownership 4500:4500 and mode 660; contents and metadata remained intact through both restarts.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and cross-node behavioral evidence. The share, mount, shared identity, ownership, directory mode, and bidirectional file semantics are correct. Both managed nodes also completed the provider-wide restart protocol and recovered fully, with lifecycle snapshots corroborating the changed boot identities.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, identities, directories, export and mount configuration, service enablement, and the restricted firewall rule were necessary implementation steps. Test-file writes were bounded evidence for cross-node behavior and restart recovery, while the scheduled restarts fulfilled the mandatory evidence protocol. The initial mount attempt contributed to discovering the missing firewall allowance and left no observed stray mount process. Final lifecycle observations show healthy package state, no failed services, no abandoned temporary files, and only task-required NFS listeners on node1. Both restart protocols include healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, mount, identity, data, and I/O; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both changes.
